question: What will the Tokyo (Ku-area) core CPI year-on-year inflation rate be for November 2026?

calls.reasoning: Anchor: October print 2.6% (status quo no change, typical monthly move ±0.1-0.3pp). Key update: the Oct-2026 index carried a larger electricity/gas subsidy (Sept-2026 usage 3.5 yen/kWh, gas 14 yen/m3; -0.35pp effect) than Oct-2025 (approx. 2.0 yen/kWh, 8 yen/m3, from memory); both drop out in November, so energy YoY rises again, adding roughly +0.1-0.2pp. Offsets: deepening rice deflation, slowing processed-food inflation (-0.05 to -0.1pp); services/hotels firm, weak yen (~160) supportive. Net central 2.7-2.8. Market check: harness found no Polymarket/Manifold market; I did not separately search Kalshi or bookmakers and found no market; no published November consensus yet.
calls.dossier:
- Oct 2026 Tokyo core (ex fresh food) +2.6% YoY (Sep +2.7%); ex fresh food & energy +2.6% (Sep +2.9%); headline +2.8%; core matched consensus 2.6 (Statistics Bureau via OANDA/Takumori note, 30 Oct 2026).
- DLRI (Oct 2026): core ex fresh food AND special factors Sep +3.0% -> Oct +3.2%; ex fresh food, energy & special factors Sep +3.0% -> Oct +2.8% (search snippet, dlri.co.jp/report/macro/672247).
- Oct 2026 energy: electricity +1.7%, city gas +4.9%, energy overall about +2.2-2.6% YoY; electricity/gas subsidy reduced the Oct index by about 0.35pp (Takumori note; OANDA).
- Summer 2026 subsidy: electricity 3.5/4.5/3.5 yen/kWh for Jul/Aug/Sep usage; city gas 14/18/14 yen/m3 (papamamamoney, May 2026). It ends with Sept usage, so the Nov 2026 index carries no subsidy.
- Summer 2025 subsidy (from memory, unverified this run): electricity about 2.0/2.4/2.0 yen/kWh, gas about 8/10/8 yen/m3 for Jul-Sep 2025 usage. The Nov 2025 index also had no subsidy; Nov 2025 Tokyo energy +2.6% YoY (Newsweek/Reuters, Nov 2025).
- So the Oct-2026 subsidy was larger than Oct-2025's, and its removal in November lifts the energy YoY rate (rough estimate +0.1-0.2pp on core).
- Nov 2025 Tokyo core +2.8% (same as Oct 2025), above the 2.7% consensus; processed-food inflation was slowing then (Reuters/Newsweek, 28 Nov 2025).
- Background (DLRI via question text): rice YoY -31.3% in Oct 2026 and deepening; food ex fresh food slowed 3.6 -> 3.0%; services +2.2%; hotels +6.7%; the water-charge special factor was already zero in Oct.
- New winter subsidy starts with Dec 2026 usage, so it does not affect the Nov index.
- Yen about 159-160/USD (16 Nov 2026), so import-cost pressure persists; BoJ December hike expected.
- Gasoline: subsidy increases from mid-Nov 2025 lowered the Nov 2025 base slightly (from memory; small weight).
- Status quo: unchanged at 2.6. Recent monthly moves were 0.1-0.3pp.
- Resolves off the Statistics Bureau mid-month preliminary Tokyo release of 27 Nov 2026 08:30 JST (生鮮食品を除く総合 YoY), not national CPI and not later revisions.
- Event window: single release on 2026-11-27 JST; survey month November 2026, about half elapsed as of 16 Nov.
- Searched but not found: a published consensus for the Nov 2026 Tokyo core print; any prediction market on it; the full DLRI Oct 2026 PDF (403).

calls.dossier:
- Oct 2026 Tokyo core (ex fresh food) +2.6% yoy (Sep +2.7%); all-items +2.8%; ex fresh food & energy +2.6% (Sep +2.9%); core s.a. m/m +0.3% (Statistics Bureau via question background, Kyodo/OANDA, 2026-10-30). Consensus for Oct was 2.6.
- Oct 2026 components: electricity yoy -2.6% -> +1.7%, city gas +4.9%, energy about +2.2-2.6% (contribution about +0.10-0.17pp); rice -31.3% yoy (record, Sep -19.8%); processed food 3.6% -> 3.0%; hotels 4.6% -> 6.7%; services +2.2%; water-charge one-off (+0.25pp in Sep) gone in Oct (DLRI/OANDA/Takumori note, Oct-Nov 2026).
- 2026 summer electricity subsidy (low voltage): Jul & Sep usage 3.5 yen/kWh, Aug usage 4.5 yen/kWh; city gas 14/18/14 yen/m3. Sep usage feeds the Oct CPI; ends after Sep usage (enechange etc., 2026).
- 2025 summer subsidy: Jul 2.0, Aug 2.4, Sep 2.0 yen/kWh (background knowledge). In Nov 2025 Tokyo energy contribution rose +0.11 -> +0.14pp as subsidies ended (DLRI Nov 2025 report).
- Implication to record: November 2026 removes a 3.5 yen/kWh subsidy vs 2.0 removed in Nov 2025, a net month-on-month energy push in Nov 2026 relative to the base (OANDA Oct-2026 review says energy shifts to the 'push-up direction' from November). Rough size: about +0.1 to +0.2pp on core (own calculation, weight-based).
- New winter subsidy: 1 yen/kWh for Dec 2026 usage, 4.5 yen/kWh for Jan-Feb 2027; does not touch the Nov index (question background).
- Nov 2025 Tokyo core +2.8% (unchanged from Oct 2025); processed food +6.5% then, signs of peaking (DLRI 2025-11). Gasoline: in Nov 2025 the gasoline subsidy was stepped up ahead of the end-2025 abolition of the provisional tax, lowering the Nov 2025 base slightly (background knowledge).
- Macro: USD/JPY about 159.7 (2026-11-16); Q3 GDP -0.1% annualized; BoJ December hike expected (news 2026-11-16).
- Downside drivers: rice deflation deepening month by month; processed-food disinflation; possible hotel normalization. Upside drivers: energy base effect, weak yen, firm services.
- Status quo: last print 2.6. Series moves in 0.1-0.3pp monthly steps.
- Resolution: off Statistics Bureau mid-month preliminary Tokyo Ku-area release, Table 1, 生鮮食品を除く総合 yoy, first print, 2026-11-27 08:30 JST; not all-items or the ex-energy series.
- Event window: survey month November 2026; release 2026-11-26 23:30 UTC; as of 2026-11-16 the mid-month survey is roughly underway; release about 10.8 days away.
- Searched, not found: market consensus for Nov 2026 Tokyo core (not yet published); DLRI Oct-2026 PDFs (403 blocked); Polymarket/Manifold market (the harness found none; Kalshi/bookmakers not searched).

calls.reasoning: Status quo 2.6 (Oct print). The larger Sep-2026-usage electricity/gas subsidy (3.5 yen/kWh vs ~2.0 in 2025) depressed Oct 2026 YoY; neither November has a subsidy, so energy adds ~+0.15pp, plus a small gasoline base effect from the Nov-2025 subsidy expansion. Offsets: rice deflation deepening and processed-food disinflation, ~-0.05 to -0.1pp. Net ~+0.1pp -> median ~2.7. No market or consensus found (harness Polymarket/Manifold search plus the runs' checks; no own search this run).
calls.reconciliation: All three runs share the same facts: Oct 2.6; the 2026 summer subsidy was larger than 2025's (the 2025 figures are from memory but consistent across runs); the winter subsidy starts with Dec usage. The disputes are judgment calls on the size of the energy base effect vs food drag. My weight-based check (~5% electricity price gap x ~3% weight ≈ 0.15pp, plus gas) supports the runs' +0.1-0.2pp; the food drag is ~0.05-0.1pp. The median is 2.7 with a slight upward lean. I kept a width of ~0.5 (Runs 1/3) over Run 2's 0.4, since monthly moves are 0.1-0.3pp. No web access this run.

disagreements.claim: Size of the energy base effect from the subsidy gap (+0.1 vs +0.2pp)

disagreements.verdict: Not verifiable without web; consistent across runs and with Nov-2025 DLRI energy contribution rising; accepted with modest uncertainty
